judgment_calls: HOLD root cause (probe 2, reproduced deterministically): sweep reachability was existence-based; a submount shadowed by a later mount over an ANCESTOR path keeps its mountpoint directory present (binfmt_misc under a fresh procfs) while the listed mount is unreachable, so the remount died EINVAL at every nested spin

Reachability now comes from the kernel: O_PATH open + /proc/self/fdinfo mnt_id mapped through mountinfo; tool survey in the reproduced topology showed findmnt -T, findmnt -M, and mountpoint(1) all table-based (they report the phantom as reachable) and st_dev colliding across same-device mounts

Fail-closed by construction: the annotator's output is captured with exit checked, empty annotation is fatal, unexpected per-target errors raise — a broken annotator refuses rather than yielding an unswept writable tree; only a can't-open path (the old [ -e ] semantics) marks a skip
python3 inside the prologue is acceptable: it is bale's own hard requirement (stdlib-only Python 3.10+), the cost is one exec per spin (~50-90ms measured), and no shell tool gives kernel truth
